Fix correctly addresses the original bug: pending transfers now reserve stock in availability calculation, admin can cancel stale pending transfers, integrity diagnostic exposes over-assigned/orphan/stuck-transfer issues.

Pre-existing 'Drabina aluminiowa 3m' (id 3343c176-...) correctly flagged is_overassigned=true (assigned 8 > total 6).
Reservation math: created TEST eq total=3, then pending transfer of 1 to FOREMAN_A -> available_quantity=2, pending_transfer_quantity=1.
POST /api/equipment/transfer-from-warehouse rejects with 400 + breakdown message containing keywords: 'calkowita', 'przypisane', 'w naprawie', 'zaginione', 'oczekujace przekazania'.
POST /api/equipment/transfers/{id}/cancel (admin) flips pending -> cancelled, freed reserved stock (pending_transfer_quantity decreased, available_quantity rose by the cancelled qty).
Cancelling an already-cancelled transfer -> 400 'Przekazanie juz rozpatrzone'.

GET /api/equipment/integrity returns object {summary, over_assigned[], orphan_assignments[], stuck_transfers[]} with summary counts matching list lengths. Known over-assigned eq present with excess>0 and all required keys (equipment_id, equipment_name, total_quantity, assigned_quantity, broken_quantity, lost_quantity, excess). Endpoint is admin-only (401/403 without token).
POST /api/equipment/integrity/repair with {cleanup_orphans:true, cancel_stuck_transfers:false} returns deleted_orphans (int) and cancelled_transfers=0.
POST /api/equipment/integrity/repair with {cancel_stuck_transfers:true} returns cancelled_transfers (int) and deleted_orphans=0.

POST /api/equipment/assign validation now subtracts pending transfers. With eq total=2 + pending=1, direct-assign 2 to another foreman rejected with 400 ('oczekujace przekazania' + 'przypisane innym'); assign 1 succeeds.

Accept flow end-to-end: warehouse -> pending -> foreman A accepts (via POST /api/auth/foreman/login then /accept) -> assigned_quantity += qty AND pending_transfer_quantity drops to 0. Used TEST_Foreman_A_a8b95c / Test1234! for foreman token.
critical_code_review_comments: set_assignment validation uses pending_qty for ALL pending transfers including ones whose to_foreman_id equals the same foreman being assigned. This is intentionally strict (forces admin to cancel/accept the pending first) but could surprise admins changing an existing assignment for a foreman who also has a pending transfer for that same equipment. Worth a UI hint, not a blocker.

cancel_transfer uses get_current_admin_or_warehouse so warehouse keepers can cancel any pending transfer (not just their own). The docstring claims 'wlasciciel transferu... tez moze odwolac' but there is no check for owner foreman; foreman cannot call this. That matches the request (admin/warehouse only) so acceptable, but the docstring is slightly misleading.
integrity_repair has no audit-trail of WHICH assignments/transfers were deleted - only counts. For destructive operations consider logging the deleted ids to equipment_history for forensic recovery.

rca of the issue: Root cause: list_equipment formerly subtracted only assigned+broken+lost from total_quantity, ignoring pending transfers. transfer-from-warehouse already reserved stock via its own pending lookup, so when admin transferred all units the next list query still showed available based on assignments (which were 0 until acceptance) BUT the validator rejected new transfers because it counted pending. UI thus showed available=0 while the equipment was not actually assigned. Fix: include pending transfers in availability computation everywhere (list, single, set_assignment) and add a cancel endpoint for admins to release reservations of stale pending transfers. Diagnostic endpoint exposes the inconsistencies so admin can repair historical data. Tests verify the math end-to-end including the accept flow that should transition pending -> assigned without double-counting.
